full_text:
Abdullah was an impoverished fisherman of Alexandria who struggled to support his wife and nine children. One morning, casting his net into the deep surf, he drew up an extraordinary creature: a merman, half human and half fish, with scales of shimmering turquoise!

The merman spoke with human speech: 'Do not slay me, brother! I am Abdullah of the Sea, even as you are Abdullah of the Land. Release me, and let us form a sacred friendship: whenever you cast your net, I shall fill it with rare oceanic pearls and rubies, and in return, you shall bring me the sweet fruits of the land—grapes, pomegranates, and figs—which grow not in the ocean depths.'

Abdullah the Fisherman released him joyfully.

For years, the extraordinary friendship flourished: every week, the fisherman brought baskets of melons, peaches, and dates to the rocky reef, and the merman emerged from the waves, presenting heavy baskets filled with pearls of peerless luster.

Abdullah the Fisherman became the wealthiest man in Egypt, yet remained humble, using his wealth to feed the poor and build schools.

One day, the merman invited Abdullah to visit the undersea cities, rubbing his eyes with magical ointment that allowed him to breathe underwater.

Exploring the palaces of coral and pearl, the fisherman was astonished to see that the mermen used diamonds and rubies merely as common pebbles to pave their garden walks, valuing them as nothing, while cherishing the sweet memory of ripe fruit!

Abdullah returned to land, enlightened by the realization that value is an illusion of scarcity: what one realm despises as common gravel, another worships as treasure, while true wealth is found only in love, friendship, and clean hands.
moral: True friendship respects the different natures of others, recognizing that gold is nothing compared to wisdom. [ES]
